text: The learner understands the concepts of extreme and relative poverty and is able to critically reflect on their underlying cultural and normative assumptions and practices.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about the local, national and global distribution of extreme poverty and extreme wealth.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about causes and impacts of poverty such as unequal distribution of resources and power, colonization, conflicts, disasters caused by natural hazards and other climate change-induced impacts, environmental degradation and technological disasters, and the lack of social protection systems and measures.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands how extremes of poverty and extremes of wealth affect basic human rights and needs.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about poverty reduction strategies and measures and is able to distinguish between deficit-based and strength-based approaches to addressing poverty.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to collaborate with others to empower individuals and communities to affect change in the distribution of power and resources in the community and beyond.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to raise awareness about extremes of poverty and wealth and encourage dialogue about solutions.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to show sensitivity to the issues of poverty as well as empathy and solidarity with poor people and those in vulnerable situations.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to identify their personal experiences and biases with respect to poverty.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to reflect critically on their own role in maintaining global structures of inequality.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to plan, implement, evaluate and replicate activities that contribute to poverty reduction.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to publicly demand and support the development and integration of policies that promote social and economic justice, risk reduction strategies and poverty eradication actions.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate, participate in and influence decision-making related to management strategies of local, national and international enterprises concerning poverty generation and eradication.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to include poverty reduction, social justice and anti-corruption considerations in their consumption activities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to propose solutions to address systemic problems related to poverty.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about hunger and malnutrition and their main physical and psychological effects on human life, and about specific vulnerable groups.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about the amount and distribution of hunger and malnutrition locally, nationally and globally, currently as well as historically.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows the main drivers and root causes for hunger at the individual, local, national and global level.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows principles of sustainable agriculture and understands the need for legal rights to have land and property as necessary conditions to promote it.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the need for sustainable agriculture to combat hunger and malnutrition worldwide and knows about other strategies to combat hunger, malnutrition and poor diets.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to communicate on the issues and connections between combating hunger and promoting sustainable agriculture and improved nutrition.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to collaborate with others to encourage and to empower them to combat hunger and to promote sustainable agriculture and improved nutrition.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to create a vision for a world without hunger and malnutrition.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to reflect on their own values and deal with diverging values, attitudes and strategies in relation to combating hunger and malnutrition and promoting sustainable agriculture.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to feel empathy, responsibility and solidarity for and with people suffering from hunger and malnutrition.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate and implement actions personally and locally to combat hunger and to promote sustainable agriculture.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate, participate in and influence decision-making related to public policies concerning the combat against hunger and malnutrition and the promotion of sustainable agriculture.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate, participate in and influence decision-making related to management strategies of local, national and international enterprises concerning the combat against hunger and malnutrition and the promotion of sustainable agriculture.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to take on critically their role as an active global citizen in the challenge of combating hunger.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to change their production and consumption practices in order to contribute to the combat against hunger and the promotion of sustainable agriculture.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows conceptions of health, hygiene and well-being and can critically reflect on them, including an understanding of the importance of gender in health and well-being.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows facts and figures about the most severe communicable and non-communicable diseases, and the most vulnerable groups and regions concerning illness, disease and premature death.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the socio-political-economic dimensions of health and well-being and knows about the effects of advertising and about strategies to promote health and well-being.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the importance of mental health. The learner understands the negative impacts of behaviours like xenophobia, discrimination and bullying on mental health and emotional well-being and how addictions to alcohol, tobacco or other drugs cause harm to health and well-being.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows relevant prevention strategies to foster positive physical and mental health and well-being, including sexual and reproductive health and information as well as early warning and risk reduction.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to interact with people suffering from illnesses, and feel empathy for their situation and feelings.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to communicate about issues of health, including sexual and reproductive health, and well-being, especially to argue in favour of prevention strategies to promote health and well-being.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to encourage others to decide and act in favour of promoting health and well-being for all.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to create a holistic understanding of a life of health and well-being, and to clarify related values, beliefs and attitudes.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to develop a personal commitment to promoting health and well-being for themselves, their family and others, including considering volunteer or professional work in health and social care.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to include health promoting behaviours in their daily routines.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to plan, implement, evaluate and replicate strategies that promote health, including sexual and reproductive health, and well-being for themselves, their families and others.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner has the capacity to perceive when others need help and to seek help for themselves and others.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to publicly demand and support the development of policies promoting health and well-being.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to propose ways to address possible conflicts between the public interest in offering medicine at affordable prices and private interests within the pharmaceutical industry.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the important role of education and lifelong learning opportunities for all (formal, non-formal and informal learning) as main drivers of sustainable development, for improving people’s lives and in achieving the SDGs.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands education as a public good, a global common good, a fundamental human right and a basis for guaranteeing the realization of other rights.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about inequality in access to and attainment of education, particularly between girls and boys and in rural areas, and about reasons for a lack of equitable access to quality education and lifelong learning opportunities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the important role of culture in achieving sustainability.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands that education can help create a more sustainable, equitable and peaceful world.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to raise awareness of the importance of quality education for all, a humanistic and holistic approach to education, ESD and related approaches.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able through participatory methods to motivate and empower others to demand and use educational opportunities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to recognize the intrinsic value of education and to analyse and identify their own learning needs in their personal development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to recognize the importance of their own skills for improving their life, in particular for employment and entrepreneurship.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to engage personally with ESD.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to contribute to facilitating and implementing quality education for all, ESD and related approaches at different levels.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to promote gender equality in education.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to publicly demand and support the development of policies promoting free, equitable and quality education for all, ESD and related approaches as well as aiming at safe, accessible and inclusive educational facilities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to promote the empowerment of young people.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to use all opportunities for their own education throughout their life, and to apply the acquired knowledge in everyday situations to promote sustainable development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the concept of gender, gender equality and gender discrimination and knows about all forms of gender discrimination, violence and inequality (e.g. harmful practices such as female genital mutilation, honour killings and child marriage, unequal employment opportunities and pay, language construction, traditional gender roles, gendered impact of natural hazards) and understands the current and historical causes of gender inequality.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the basic rights of women and girls, including their right to freedom from exploitation and violence and their reproductive rights.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands levels of gender equality within their own country and culture in comparison to global norms (while respecting cultural sensitivity), including the intersectionality of gender with other social categories such as ability, religion and race.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows the opportunities and benefits provided by full gender equality and participation in legislation and governance, including public budget allocation, the labour market and public and private decision-making.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the role of education, enabling technology and legislation in empowering and ensuring the full participation of all genders.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to recognize and question traditional perception of gender roles in a critical approach, while respecting cultural sensitivity.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to identify and speak up against all forms of gender discrimination and debate the benefits of full empowerment of all genders.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to connect with others who work to end gender discrimination and violence, empower those who may still be disempowered and promote respect and full equality on all levels.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to reflect on their own gender identity and gender roles.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to feel empathy and solidarity with those who differ from personal or community gender expectations and roles.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to take the measure of their surroundings to empower themselves or others who are discriminated against because of their gender.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate, participate in and influence decision-making about gender equality and participation.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to support others in developing empathy across genders and breaking down gender discrimination and violence.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to observe and identify gender discrimination.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to plan, implement, support and evaluate strategies for gender equality.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands water as a fundamental condition of life itself, the importance of water quality and quantity, and the causes, effects and consequences of water pollution and water scarcity.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands that water is part of many different complex global interrelationships and systems.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about the global unequal distribution of access to safe drinking water and sanitation facilities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the concept of “virtual water”.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the concept of Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) and other strategies for ensuring the availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation, including flood and drought risk management.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to participate in activities of improving water and sanitation management in local communities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to communicate about water pollution, water access and water saving measures and to create visibility about success stories.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to feel responsible for their water use.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to see the value in good sanitation and hygiene standards.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to question socio-economic differences as well as gender disparities in the access to safe drinking water and sanitation facilities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to cooperate with local authorities in the improvement of local capacity for self-sufficiency.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to contribute to water resources management at the local level.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to reduce their individual water footprint and to save water practicing their daily habits.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to plan, implement, evaluate and replicate activities that contribute to increasing water quality and safety.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate, participate in and influence decision-making on management strategies of local, national and international enterprises related to water pollution.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about different energy resources – renewable and non-renewable – and their respective advantages and disadvantages including environmental impacts, health issues, usage, safety and energy security, and their share in the energy mix at the local, national and global level.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows what energy is primarily used for in different regions of the world.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the concept of energy efficiency and sufficiency and knows socio-technical strategies and policies to achieve efficiency and sufficiency.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands how policies can influence the development of energy production, supply, demand and usage.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about harmful impacts of unsustainable energy production, understands how renewable energy technologies can help to drive sustainable development and understands the need for new and innovative technologies and especially technology transfer in collaborations between countries.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to communicate the need for energy efficiency and sufficiency.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to assess and understand the need for affordable, reliable, sustainable and clean energy of other people/other countries or regions.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to cooperate and collaborate with others to transfer and adapt energy technologies to different contexts and to share energy best practices of their communities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to clarify personal norms and values related to energy production and usage as well as to reflect and evaluate their own energy usage in terms of efficiency and sufficiency.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to develop a vision of a reliable, sustainable energy production, supply and usage in their country.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to apply and evaluate measures in order to increase energy efficiency and sufficiency in their personal sphere and to increase the share of renewable energy in their local energy mix.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to apply basic principles to determine the most appropriate renewable energy strategy in a given situation.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to analyse the impact and long-term effects of big energy projects (e.g. constructing an off-shore wind park) and energy related policies on different stakeholder groups (including nature).
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to influence public policies related to energy production, supply and usage.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to compare and assess different business models and their suitability for different energy solutions and to influence energy suppliers to produce safe, reliable and sustainable energy.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the concepts of sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment, and decent work, including the advancement of gender parity and equality, and knows about alternative economic models and indicators.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner has knowledge about the distribution of formal employment rates per sector, informal employment, and unemployment in different world regions or nations, and which social groups are especially affected by unemployment.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the relation between employment and economic growth, and knows about other moderating factors like a growing labour force or new technologies that substitute jobs.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands how low and decreasing wages for the labour force and very high wages and profits of managers and owners or shareholders are leading to inequalities, poverty, civil unrest, etc.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands how innovation, entrepreneurship and new job creation can contribute to decent work and a sustainability-driven economy and to the decoupling of economic growth from the impacts of natural hazards and environmental degradation.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to discuss economic models and future visions of economy and society critically and to communicate them in public spheres.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to collaborate with others to demand fair wages, equal pay for equal work and labour rights from politicians and from their employer.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to understand how one’s own consumption affects working conditions of others in the global economy.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to identify their individual rights and clarify their needs and values related to work.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to develop a vision and plans for their own economic life based on an analysis of their competencies and contexts.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to engage with new visions and models of a sustainable, inclusive economy and decent work.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to facilitate improvements related to unfair wages, unequal pay for equal work and bad working conditions.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to develop and evaluate ideas for sustainability-driven innovation and entrepreneurship.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to plan and implement entrepreneurial projects.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to develop criteria and make responsible consumption choices as a means to support fair working conditions and efforts to decouple production from the impact of natural hazards and environmental degradation.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the concepts of sustainable infrastructure and industrialization and society’s needs for a systemic approach to their development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the local, national and global challenges and conflicts in achieving sustainability in infrastructure and industrialization.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner can define the term resilience in the context of infrastructure and spatial planning, understanding key concepts such as modularity and diversity, and apply it to their local community and nationwide.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows the pitfalls of unsustainable industrialization and in contrast knows examples of resilient, inclusive, sustainable industrial development and the need for contingency planning.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is aware of new opportunities and markets for sustainability innovation, resilient infrastructure and industrial development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to argue for sustainable, resilient and inclusive infrastructure in their local area.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to encourage their communities to shift their infrastructure and industrial development toward more resilient and sustainable forms.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to find collaborators to develop sustainable and contextual industries that respond to our shifting challenges and also to reach new markets.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to recognize and reflect on their own personal demands on the local infrastructure such as their carbon and water footprints and food miles.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to understand that with changing resource availability (e. g. peak oil, peak everything) and other external shocks and stresses (e. g. natural hazards, conflicts) their own perspective and demands on infrastructure may need to shift radically regarding availability of renewable energy for ICT, transport options, sanitation options, etc.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to identify opportunities in their own culture and nation for greener and more resilient approaches to infrastructure, understanding their overall benefits for societies, especially with regard to disaster risk reduction.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate various forms of industrialization and compare their resilience.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to innovate and develop sustainable enterprises to respond to their countries’ industrial needs.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to access financial services such as loans or microfinance to support their own enterprises.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to work with decision-makers to improve the uptake of sustainable infrastructure (including internet access).
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows different dimensions of inequality, their interrelations and applicable statistics.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows indicators that measure and describe inequalities and understands their relevance for decision-making.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands that inequality is a major driver for societal problems and individual dissatisfaction.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands local, national and global processes that both promote and hinder equality (fiscal, wage, and social protection policies, corporate activities, etc. ).
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands ethical principles concerning equality and is aware of psychological processes that foster discriminative behaviour and decision making.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to raise awareness about inequalities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to feel empathy for and to show solidarity with people who are discriminated against.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to negotiate the rights of different groups based on shared values and ethical principles.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner becomes aware of inequalities in their surroundings as well as in the wider world and is able to recognize the problematic consequences.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to maintain a vision of a just and equal world.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate inequalities in their local environment in terms of quality (different dimensions, qualitative impact on individuals) and quantity (indicators, quantitative impact on individuals).
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to identify or develop an objective indicator to compare different groups, nations, etc. with respect to inequalities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to identify and analyse different types of causes and reasons for inequalities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to plan, implement and evaluate strategies to reduce inequalities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to engage in the development of public policies and corporate activities that reduce inequalities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands basic physical, social and psychological human needs and is able to identify how these needs are currently addressed in their own physical urban, peri-urban and rural settlements.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate and compare the sustainability of their and other settlements’ systems in meeting their needs particularly in the areas of food, energy, transport, water, safety, waste treatment, inclusion and accessibility, education, integration of green spaces and disaster risk reduction.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the historical reasons for settlement patterns and while respecting cultural heritage, understands the need to find compromises to develop improved sustainable systems.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows the basic principles of sustainable planning and building, and can identify opportunities for making their own area more sustainable and inclusive.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the role of local decision-makers and participatory governance and the importance of representing a sustainable voice in planning and policy for their area.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to use their voice, to identify and use entry points for the public in the local planning systems, to call for the investment in sustainable infrastructure, buildings and parks in their area and to debate the merits of long-term planning.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to connect with and help community groups locally and online in developing a sustainable future vision of their community.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to reflect on their region in the development of their own identity, understanding the roles that the natural, social and technical environments have had in building their identity and culture.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to contextualize their needs within the needs of the greater surrounding ecosystems, both locally and globally, for more sustainable human settlements.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to feel responsible for the environmental and social impacts of their own individual lifestyle.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to plan, implement and evaluate community-based sustainability projects.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to participate in and influence decision processes about their community.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to speak against/for and to organize their voice against/for decisions made for their community.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to co-create an inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable community.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to promote low carbon approaches at the local level.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands how individual lifestyle choices influence social, economic and environmental development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands production and consumption patterns and value chains and the interrelatedness of production and consumption (supply and demand, toxics, CO2 emissions, waste generation, health, working conditions, poverty, etc. ).
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows roles, rights and duties of different actors in production and consumption (media and advertising, enterprises, municipalities, legislation, consumers, etc. ).
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about strategies and practices of sustainable production and consumption.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands dilemmas/trade-offs related to and system changes necessary for achieving sustainable consumption and production.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to communicate the need for sustainable practices in production and consumption.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to encourage others to engage in sustainable practices in consumption and production.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to differentiate between needs and wants and to reflect on their own individual consumer behaviour in light of the needs of the natural world, other people, cultures and countries, and future generations.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to envision sustainable lifestyles.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to feel responsible for the environmental and social impacts of their own individual behaviour as a producer or consumer.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to plan, implement and evaluate consumption-related activities using existing sustainability criteria.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate, participate in and influence decision-making processes about acquisitions in the public sector.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to promote sustainable production patterns.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able take on critically on their role as an active stakeholder in the market.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to challenge cultural and societal orientations in consumption and production.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the greenhouse effect as a natural phenomenon caused by an insulating layer of greenhouse gases.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the current climate change as an anthropogenic phenomenon resulting from increased greenhouse gas emissions.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows which human activities – on a global, national, local and individual level – contribute most to climate change.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about the main ecological, social, cultural and economic consequences of climate change locally, nationally and globally and understands how these can themselves become catalysing, reinforcing factors for climate change.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about prevention, mitigation and adaptation strategies at different levels (global to individual) and for different contexts and their connections with disaster response and disaster risk reduction.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to explain ecosystem dynamics and the environmental, social, economic and ethical impact of climate change.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to encourage others to protect the climate.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to collaborate with others and to develop commonly agreed-upon strategies to deal with climate change.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to understand their personal impact on the world’s climate, from a local to a global perspective.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to recognize that the protection of the global climate is an essential task for everyone and that we need to completely re-evaluate our worldview and everyday behaviours in light of this.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to evaluate whether their private and job activities are climate friendly and – where not – to revise them.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to act in favour of people threatened by climate change.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to anticipate, estimate and assess the impact of personal, local and national decisions or activities on other people and world regions.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to promote climate-protecting public policies.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to support climate-friendly economic activities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands basic marine ecology, ecosystems, predator-prey relationships, etc.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the connection of many people to the sea and the life it holds, including the sea’s role as a provider of food, jobs and exciting opportunities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows the basic premise of climate change and the role of the oceans in moderating our climate.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands threats to ocean systems such as pollution and overfishing and recognizes and can explain the relative fragility of many ocean ecosystems including coral reefs and hypoxic dead zones.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows about opportunities for the sustainable use of living marine resources.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to argue for sustainable fishing practices.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to show people the impact humanity is having on the oceans (biomass loss, acidification, pollution, etc.) and the value of clean healthy oceans.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to influence groups that engage in unsustainable production and consumption of ocean products.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to reflect on their own dietary needs and question whether their dietary habits make sustainable use of limited resources of seafood.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to empathize with people whose livelihoods are affected by changing fishing practices.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to research their country’s dependence on the sea.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to debate sustainable methods such as strict fishing quotas and moratoriums on species in danger of extinction.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to identify, access and buy sustainably harvested marine life, e.g. ecolabel certified products.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to contact their representatives to discuss overfishing as a threat to local livelihoods.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to campaign for expanding no-fish zones and marine reserves and for their protection on a scientific basis.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands basic ecology with reference to local and global ecosystems, identifying local species and understanding the measure of biodiversity.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the manifold threats posed to biodiversity, including habitat loss, deforestation, fragmentation, overexploitation and invasive species, and can relate these threats to their local biodiversity.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to classify the ecosystem services of the local ecosystems including supporting, provisioning, regulating and cultural services and ecosystems services for disaster risk reduction.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the slow regeneration of soil and the multiple threats that are destroying and removing it much faster than it can replenish itself, such as poor farming or forestry practice.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands that realistic conservation strategies work outside pure nature reserves to also improve legislation, restore degraded habitats and soils, connect wildlife corridors, sustainable agriculture and forestry, and redress humanity’s relationship to wildlife.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to argue against destructive environmental practices that cause biodiversity loss.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to argue for the conservation of biodiversity on multiple grounds including ecosystems services and intrinsic value.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to connect with their local natural areas and feel empathy with non-human life on Earth.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to question the dualism of human/nature and realizes that we are a part of nature and not apart from nature.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to create a vision of a life in harmony with nature.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to connect with local groups working toward biodiversity conservation in their area.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to effectively use their voice effectively in decision-making processes to help urban and rural areas become more permeable to wildlife through the establishment of wildlife corridors, agro-environmental schemes, restoration ecology and more.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to work with policy-makers to improve legislation for biodiversity and nature conservation, and its implementation.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to highlight the importance of soil as our growing material for all food and the importance of remediating or stopping the erosion of our soils.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to campaign for international awareness of species exploitation and work for the implementation and development of CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) regulations.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands concepts of justice, inclusion and peace and their relationship to law.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands their local and national legislative and governance systems, how they represent them and that they can be abused through corruption.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to compare their system of justice with those of other countries.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the importance of individuals and groups in upholding justice, inclusion and peace and supporting strong institutions in their country and globally.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the importance of the international human rights framework.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to connect with others who can help them in facilitating peace, justice, inclusion and strong institutions in their country.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to debate local and global issues of peace, justice, inclusion and strong institutions.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to show empathy with and solidarity for those suffering from injustice in their own country as well as in other countries.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to reflect on their role in issues of peace, justice, inclusion and strong institutions.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to reflect on their own personal belonging to diverse groups (gender, social, economic, political, ethnical, national, ability, sexual orientation etc.) their access to justice and their shared sense of humanity.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to critically assess issues of peace, justice, inclusion and strong institutions in their region, nationally and globally.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to publicly demand and support the development of policies promoting peace, justice, inclusion and strong institutions.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to collaborate with groups that are currently experiencing injustice and/or conflicts.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to become an agent of change in local decision-making, speaking up against injustice.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to contribute to conflict resolution at the local and national level.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands global issues, including issues of financing for development, taxation, debt and trade policies, and the interconnectedness and interdependency of different countries and populations.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner understands the importance of global multi-stakeholder partnerships and the shared accountability for sustainable development and knows examples of networks, institutions, campaigns of global partnerships.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows the concepts of global governance and global citizenship.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner recognizes the importance of cooperation on and access to science, technology and innovation, and knowledge sharing.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner knows concepts for measuring progress on sustainable development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to raise awareness about the importance of global partnerships for sustainable development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to work with others to promote global partnerships for sustainable development and demand governments’ accountability for the SDGs.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to take ownership of the SDGs.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to create a vision for a sustainable global society.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to experience a sense of belonging to a common humanity, sharing values and responsibilities, based on human rights.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to become a change agent to realize the SDGs and to take on their role as an active, critical and global and sustainability citizen.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to contribute to facilitating and implementing local, national and global partnerships for sustainable development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to publicly demand and support the development of policies promoting global partnerships for sustainable development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to support development cooperation activities.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective

text: The learner is able to influence companies to become part of global partnerships for sustainable development.
:LABEL: ESDLearningObjective
